note: Fragments read: Edson Keith, merchant of Edson Keith & Company, suffered for at least a decade from insomnia and dyspepsia; on Monday 21 September 1896 he left his house in the early morning, walked to the lake at the foot of 16th Street and drowned himself; the papers said he 'committed suicide Monday morning by drowning himself in Lake Michigan'. The page does not give his Prairie Avenue number. Read whole (T-3606): he spent another sleepless night pacing the hallways, and his butler found him in a state of deliriousness at 2 AM; a hat and coat were found on the beach on Monday morning, and the household staff realised what had happened only from the Tuesday newspaper; fishermen on the beach told what they had seen. A few weeks before, his brother Elbridge and his wife had spoken with Mrs. Keith, who said, 'I … suspect that he was losing control of his mind through long suffering.' His personal secretary had never heard him say anything nasty or unkind about anyone. The firm, founded in 1858 by Osborn R. Keith and Albert Faxon on Lake Street, became Edson Keith & Company, with annual sales of $4.5 million in the mid-1880s, over 200 employees in Chicago and 500 more in a Milwaukee factory. His will of 13 March 1895 left $300,000 each to his wife Susan and to his sons Edson, Jr. and Walter W.
